admin.title: Admin
admin.desc: System health, jobs, audit, quotas and maintenance.
admin.jobsDesc: Core's periodic background jobs (Reaper, ledger, price feed…).
admin.adminKeyDesc: Admin keys see and control every box. Agent keys are created on the agent page.
admin.revokeAdminDesc: This is an admin key. If the dashboard uses it, you'll be signed out.
admin.revokeAgentDesc: Agents using this key lose access immediately.
admin.quotasDesc: Hard limits in Core — agents get POLICY_DENIED when they exceed them.
admin.gpuHint: Moved out of v1, planned for phase P5
admin.maintenanceDesc: When on: a banner shows on every page and Core refuses new boxes (running boxes keep running).
admin.usersNote: Boxaz v1 is for a single operator. Dashboard access = an admin key (managed in the API keys tab).

agentDetail.newKeyDesc: The key only sees this agent's boxes.
agentDetail.revokeDesc: Agents using this key get UNAUTHORIZED immediately.
agentDetail.noBoxes: This agent hasn't created any boxes
agentDetail.connectDesc: Config per transport — paste it into the agent along with BOXAZ_API_KEY.

agents.title: Agents
agents.desc: Each agent has its own keys, budget and policy.
agents.createDesc: Three steps, then you get a key and a config snippet to paste into the agent.
agents.emptyDesc: Create your first agent to get an API key.

apiErrors.notLoggedInHint: Open /login and enter an admin API key.
apiErrors.invalidKey: The API key is invalid or lacks admin scope
apiErrors.invalidKeyHint: Create an admin-scope key with `box keys create --admin`.

approvals.emptyDesc: When an agent passes 80% of its budget, a service is about to stop, or more hosts are needed, requests show up here.

boxActions.deleteDesc: The box and its disk are deleted permanently. Saved snapshots are kept per the Reaper policy.

boxDetail.errorRetries: Error (after {n, plural, one {# try} other {# tries}})
boxDetail.whyHere: Why the Scheduler placed it here

timeline.tokensTitle: Tokens saved for the agent by trimming output

files.pickDesc: /work is the working folder; /memory is the agent's long-term memory (kept across sleeps).

logs.hint: Full logs are stored under the <mono>log_id</mono> the agent gets in the exec result (when output is truncated).
logs.journalTitle: Box event journal ({n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}})

snapshots.emptyDesc: The Reaper snapshots a box when it puts it to sleep.
snapshots.restoreDesc: The box's current state is replaced by this snapshot. Take a fresh snapshot first if you need to keep it.
snapshots.forkDesc: Creates a new box with the same spec from this snapshot; the current box is untouched.
snapshots.storageLocalHint: Restorable only on the host that took it.

config.rebuilt: rebuilt from box details (Core has no /yaml yet)
config.saveTemplateDesc: Agents can create an identical box with <mono>template: {name}</mono>.

boxes.title: Boxes
boxes.desc: Every box your agents use, across every provider.
boxes.emptyDesc: Agents create boxes on their own through the API or MCP.

common.copyFailed: The browser blocked the clipboard — select and copy manually
common.name: Name

costs.title: Costs
costs.desc: Itemized ledger by agent, task, provider and day.
costs.poolDesc: Share of monthly host cost allocated to boxes
costs.burstDesc: Hourly hosts rented when the pool is full

createBox.title: Create a box manually
createBox.desc: Agents usually create boxes themselves. Use this for a quick test or a rescue.
createBox.quoteStale: Settings changed — quote again to refresh.
createBox.noAlternatives: No other option fits the policy.
createBox.pickAgentFirst: Pick an agent to quote against its policy.
createBox.descNeed: Describe what the box needs; Boxaz ranks the options by price, speed and reliability.

developers.title: For agents
developers.desc: Everything an agent needs to connect to Boxaz on its own: machine-readable docs, tool schemas, sample calls and the error table.
developers.discoveryDesc: Hand these links to an agent: it reads them and knows what to call. Discovery endpoints need no API key.

items.openapiDesc: Every REST endpoint, schema and error code. Generate clients or load it into an agent.
items.llmsDesc: Short summary for LLMs: how to connect, rules of thumb, tool list.
items.llmsFullDesc: Full version with every endpoint's schema — load it once and you're set.
items.a2aDesc: /.well-known/agent.json: lets other agents hand tasks to Boxaz via /a2a.

developers.toolsDesc: GET /v1/tools?format=… returns the same tool set in each model vendor's format.
developers.quickstartDesc: Quote → create → run → wait for the job → read the log → delete. Replace BOX_ID, JOB_ID, LOG_ID with returned values.
developers.sdkDesc: Install once; configure with BOXAZ_URL and BOXAZ_API_KEY.
developers.sdkNote: SDK package names are provisional — confirm when Core publishes them.
developers.errorsDesc: Agents read <mono>code</mono> (never changes) and follow <mono>hint</mono>; <mono>message</mono>/<mono>hint</mono> are localized via Accept-Language; honor <mono>retry_after_s</mono> when present.

errs.BUDGET_EXCEEDED: The agent or box is out of budget.
errs.BUDGET_EXCEEDEDHint: Stop creating boxes; wait for the next day (00:00 UTC) or ask the operator to approve more.
errs.NO_CAPACITY: No capacity matching the policy right now.
errs.PROVIDER_FAILED: The cloud provider failed or its token is broken.
errs.PROVIDER_FAILEDHint: Retry later; if it repeats, tell the operator to check the provider token.
errs.BOX_SLEEPINGHint: Call wake (or exec, which wakes it) and run again.
errs.TIMEOUTHint: Use async=true with GET /v1/jobs/JOB_ID?wait=30, or raise timeout_s.
errs.POLICY_DENIED: Policy or quota violation (provider, region, egress, box count, maintenance, human takeover).
errs.POLICY_DENIEDHint: Read the specific hint; change the request to fit the policy instead of retrying as is.
errs.NOT_FOUNDHint: Call box_list (or the matching list) to get the right ID.
errs.UNAUTHORIZEDHint: Check BOXAZ_API_KEY; don't retry in a loop.
errs.INVALIDHint: Fix what the message points to (usually a field or line) and resend.
errs.RATE_LIMITEDHint: Wait retry_after_s; batch commands with box_exec_batch.
errs.INTERNALHint: Retry once; if it persists, stop and tell the operator.
errs.NO_CAPACITYHint: Lower the spec, wait retry_after_s and retry, or call box_quote for alternatives.

developers.a2aDesc: Other agents send JSON-RPC to <mono>/a2a</mono>: a text part is a command (with <mono>metadata.box_id</mono>), a data part with <mono>tool</mono> + <mono>arguments</mono> calls any tool. A command's task id is its job id.

a2aMethods.message_send: Runs a command or tool, waits up to 30 s, returns the Task.
a2aMethods.message_stream: Same, streamed as SSE until done.
a2aMethods.tasks_cancel: Cancels a running job (kills the command).
a2aMethods.tasks_resubscribe: Re-attach to a running task's SSE.

emergency.title: Emergency stop
emergency.step1: Every running or provisioning box goes to sleep right away (with a snapshot). Agents get BOX_SLEEPING errors until you wake them again.
emergency.step2: Step 2/2 — type {word} to confirm. This applies to every agent.
emergency.done: Put {n, plural, one {# box} other {# boxes}} to sleep. Nothing is burning compute now.

infra.title: Infrastructure
infra.desc: Providers, pool hosts and market prices.
infra.addHostDesc: Billed monthly; the Scheduler places boxes on it while there's room.
infra.drainDesc: The host stops taking new boxes; running boxes move to other hosts as they sleep and wake.
infra.deleteDesc: Destroys the machine at the provider. Only possible when no box is running on it.
infra.unverifiedNote: “Unverified” offers are always self-tested before the Scheduler uses them for real.
infra.chainHint: Order the Scheduler tries when it needs a burst host. The first connected provider wins.
infra.envTokenHint: Set via Core environment variables. Pasting a new token here overrides it until the next restart.
infra.localHint: Hosts register themselves with boxd and a bootstrap token; no API token needed.

tokenHint.contabo: Paste client_id:client_secret:api_user:api_password (or the 4-field JSON) from Contabo's API page.
tokenHint.netcup: Paste an SCP refresh token (client scp). Name spare servers boxaz-spare-1; Boxaz claims and reinstalls them.
tokenHint.digitalocean: Personal access token with read and write scope.
tokenHint.hetzner: Read & Write API token of the Hetzner Cloud project.
tokenHint.vultr: API key with the manage_servers permission.

categoryDesc.coding: IDEs and CLIs that write code — connect over MCP
categoryDesc.framework: Agent libraries — MCP, SDK or function calling
categoryDesc.workflow: Automation flows — call REST or MCP
categoryDesc.platform: Ready-made assistants — add an MCP server

kinds.genericHint: {kind} doesn't list this transport — below is the generic version, which still works.

locale.label: Language
locale.dashboardHint: Stored in this browser's boxaz_locale cookie. Errors from Core come back in this language too.
locale.notify: Default language for notifications & API errors
locale.notifyHint: Used for Telegram, email and agents that send no Accept-Language.

login.title: Sign in to Boxaz
login.subtitle: Use an API key with admin scope
login.keyHint: Create one with <mono>box keys create --admin</mono>. The key lives in an httpOnly cookie, never in JavaScript.
login.mock: MOCK MODE — enter without a key

meta.description: Personal cloud infrastructure for AI agents

onboarding.title: First-time setup
onboarding.desc: About 5 minutes: connect a provider, build a host, create an agent and wait for its first call.
onboarding.tokenDesc: Hetzner is the main pool: cheapest for long-running boxes. Create a token in Hetzner Console → Project → Security → API tokens with Read & Write permission.
onboarding.tokenHint: The token is stored in Core's Secrets and never shown again in the UI.

phases.api: Calling the Hetzner API to create the machine

onboarding.hostDesc: One monthly machine; the Scheduler packs many boxes onto it, so each extra box costs almost nothing.
onboarding.agentDesc: The agent gets an API key and a config snippet for its kind (Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph, n8n, Hark…).
onboarding.successDesc: The agent just made its first call. From now on it creates boxes, runs commands and sleeps idle boxes itself; you just watch and approve.
onboarding.waiting: Waiting for the agent's first call…
onboarding.waitingDesc: Paste the config into <mono>{name}</mono>, then ask it to run <mono>box_list</mono> or create a box. This screen moves on when Boxaz receives the call.

overview.title: Overview
overview.desc: What it costs, what's running, what needs you.
overview.savedDesc: Thanks to the Reaper sleeping idle boxes and pool placement

palette.title: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Type a command: wake shopee, sleep kecon, kill all, cost today…
palette.emptyVerb: No box to {verb, select, wake {wake} other {put to sleep}} matches “{term}”
palette.costToast: Spent {spent} of the {budget} daily budget today

aliases.developers: openapi mcp llms tools api agent sdk

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.desc: Names only. Values never leave Core.
secrets.addDesc: The value is encrypted and never shown again in the UI.
secrets.rotateDesc: New boxes get the new value immediately; running boxes get it when they wake again.
secrets.hint: Secrets are injected into a box as environment variables when the agent declares <mono>secrets: [NAME]</mono>.
secrets.deleteDesc: New boxes won't get this variable. Running boxes keep the old value until they sleep.

settings.title: Settings
settings.desc: Language, notifications, storage, Reaper, network, domain and budget.
settings.reaperDesc: Applied when the agent doesn't declare its own.
settings.domainDesc: v1 uses free sslip.io + HTTPS. With your own domain, just change this value.
settings.urlToken: Protect box URLs with a token
settings.urlTokenHint: Adds ?t=… to the URL so strangers can't open it
settings.tunnel: Allow in-box tunnels for public URLs
settings.tunnelHint: When a sandbox provider has no preview URL and Core is not reachable from the internet, a free Cloudflare quick tunnel runs inside the box (URL can change after a wake)
settings.networkDesc: Each box's allowlist lives on the box page. This is the default for boxes that declare none.
settings.egressDenyHint: Boxes without an egress policy may only reach their agent's allowlist; with no allowlist everything is blocked.

confidence.stock_limitedHint: This provider often runs out of stock here

templates.title: Templates
templates.desc: Reusable box.yaml blueprints. Agents call box_up with template: template-name.
templates.deleteDesc: Running boxes aren't affected; agents can no longer create new boxes from this template.

terminal.mockWatching: # Watching agent {agent}. Pick “Control” to type commands.
terminal.mockHelp: Mock commands: ls [path], cat [file], pwd, whoami, clear; anything else goes through /exec
terminal.wsFailed: # Couldn't open a WebSocket to Core.
terminal.wsFailedHint: # Check: the dashboard origin is in Core's allowlist (BOXAZ_DASHBOARD_URL or BOXAZ_ACCESS_ORIGINS), Core has the right BOXAZ_PUBLIC_URL (or set NEXT_PUBLIC_BOXAZ_WS), and the ticket is under 60 seconds old.
terminal.takeoverToast: You have the terminal. The agent's exec is paused.
terminal.notRunning: The box isn't running — create or restore it to use the terminal.
terminal.mockTicket: # Ticket {prefix}… (single use, 60 s) — the API key stays on the dashboard server
terminal.newSessionLine: # New session {id} · kept {ttl} if the connection drops
terminal.wakeLine: # The box is asleep — waking it, the first connection can take a few seconds…
terminal.reconnecting: # Disconnected ({why}) — retrying in {s}s (attempt {n}) with a fresh ticket
terminal.controlLost: # Another viewer took control — you are now view only
terminal.modeControlLine: # Control mode: keystrokes go to the session
terminal.modeViewLine: # View-only mode: keystrokes are not sent
terminal.takeoverHint: Pause the agent's exec in the box while you work
terminal.killDesc: The shell in this session is stopped and everyone watching is disconnected.
terminal.wakeNotice: The box is asleep. Opening the terminal wakes it (usually a few seconds) and keeps it awake while the session is open.
terminal.mockNotice: MOCK: tickets and the session list are simulated; WebSockets don't run through the mock proxy, so the shell is simulated over /exec.
terminal.footer: Sessions keep running {ttl} after a drop; reopening reattaches with the output you missed. Every connection uses a fresh single-use ticket.

wizard.name: Agent name
wizard.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Example: shopee-crawler
wizard.egressHint: One domain per line, * supported. Empty = allow every destination.
wizard.keyOnce: The API key is shown only once
wizard.keyOnceDesc: Copy and store it now. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one on the agent page.
wizard.envStep: 1. Set environment variables where the agent runs

egress.title: Egress
egress.editDesc: One domain, IP or CIDR per line, optionally with :port. With a list, every other destination is blocked.
egress.denyDefaultHint: On with an empty list = the box has no Internet access.
egress.emptyMeans: Empty with blocking off falls back to the agent or settings default.
egress.unrestricted: Unrestricted: the box can reach any address.
egress.offline: Empty list: the box has no Internet access.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.desc: Daily cost report and alerts via a Telegram bot and email. Tokens and passwords are encrypted in the secrets store and never shown again.
notify.secretStored: Stored (encrypted). Leave empty to keep it.
notify.saveFirst: Test buttons use the saved settings, so save first.

storage.title: Snapshot storage
storage.desc: Snapshots are uploaded to Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or S3 so they can be restored and forked on any host. Unconfigured, they stay on the host that took them.
storage.regionHint: R2: auto. B2: taken from the endpoint.
storage.secretStored: Stored (encrypted). Leave empty to keep it.
storage.localDesc: Snapshots stay on the host that took them and can only be restored or forked there.
storage.retentionNote: Keeps {keep} snapshots per box and deletes them after {days} days (set in Reaper). Bucket copies are deleted too.

help.cost: Expected total cost relative to the cheapest option
help.speed: Time until the box is running
help.latency: Estimated round trip from the agent to the region
help.capacity: Capacity left after placing the box

breakerHelp.closed: Normal: Boxaz calls this provider as usual
breakerHelp.half_open: Trying one call to see whether the provider has recovered
breakerHelp.open: Skipped after repeated failures; Boxaz fails over to the next provider

wizard.title: Connect a provider
wizard.desc: Pick a provider, paste a token; Boxaz checks it, then you set priority and cost caps.
wizard.keepToken: Leave empty to re-check the stored token

where.hetzner: Hetzner Console → Security → API tokens → Generate (Read & Write).
where.vultr: Vultr → Account → API → Enable API, and allow Core's IP.
where.digitalocean: DigitalOcean → API → Generate New Token (write scope).
where.contabo: Contabo: paste client_id:client_secret:user:password from Customer Control Panel → API.
where.netcup: netcup SCP → Options → API: paste customer_number:api_key:api_password.

wizard.regions: {n, plural, one {# usable region} other {# usable regions}}
wizard.groupVpsDesc: Rent servers by the hour or month; many boxes per host.
wizard.groupSandboxDesc: One sandbox per box, billed per second, deleted when the box ends.
wizard.sandboxBilling: Prices are shown per hour for comparison; you are billed per second while the sandbox runs.

prefs.title: {name} settings
prefs.desc: Priority and cost caps used when Boxaz rents servers on its own.
prefs.enabledHint: Turn off to make Boxaz skip this provider when placing boxes.

health.title: Provider health
health.desc: Core probes each provider API on a schedule and records latency, errors and server provisioning time. Repeated failures open the breaker so Boxaz fails over to the next provider.
health.breakerInfo: {n, plural, one {# failure in a row} other {# failures in a row}} · reason: {reason}
health.scoreHint: Score for a reference 1 vCPU / 1 GB box, from the same engine as Recommend.
health.noScore: No score yet: needs a connected token and prices.
health.resetHint: Close the breaker so Boxaz uses this provider again right away

cat.title: Merged price catalog
cat.desc: Community price feed merged with live prices from connected provider APIs. Live API prices win; old sources are flagged.
cat.staleNote: {n, plural, one {# source is stale} other {# sources are stale}}
cat.perSecondHint: Sandboxes bill per second; no monthly price
cat.adapterPriceHint: Per-second rates from the adapter (provider pricing page)

mesh.title: WireGuard mesh (headscale)
mesh.desc: Hosts and service boxes reach each other over a private WireGuard network; ACLs are generated from agents and box ports.
mesh.disabledHint: Set BOXAZ_MESH_URL and BOXAZ_MESH_API_KEY for Core to turn it on.
mesh.keyDesc: A one-time key that lets a host or box join the mesh with the right tags.
mesh.runOnNode: Run on the machine that should join:
mesh.keyOnce: The key is shown only once. Copy it now.

speed.title: Start-up speed
speed.cacheEnv: {n, plural, one {# package cache variable} other {# package cache variables}}
speed.warmDesc: Keep a few started containers per template so new boxes are claimed in about a second. Min is always kept, max is the cap, TTL is how long a warm container is kept before it is replaced.
speed.invalid: Each pool needs a template, 0 ≤ min ≤ max ≤ 10 and a TTL of 5–1440 minutes.
speed.rsEmpty: No box has enough data yet

rec.title: Recommend a box
rec.desc: Describe the job; Boxaz compares the warm pool, existing pool hosts, VMs and new servers, then ranks them on six explained factors.
rec.regionHint: Leave empty to let Boxaz choose
rec.pickAgent: Pick an agent to create the box.
rec.rejected: {n, plural, one {# rejected option} other {# rejected options}}

general.name: General
general.desc: Small all-purpose Linux box for scripts and quick experiments.

coding-agent.name: Coding agent
coding-agent.desc: Repo work (git, builds, tests). Fast start and low latency matter most.

browser-automation.name: Browser automation
browser-automation.desc: Headless Chromium/Playwright scraping and web tasks; needs RAM and outbound access.

build.name: Build / CI
build.desc: Short CPU-heavy compiles and tests; cheapest compute that finishes soon, then thrown away.

data.name: Data processing
data.desc: Pandas/DuckDB/ETL jobs: RAM and disk heavy, latency-insensitive.

long-running-service.name: Long-running service
long-running-service.desc: Bots, webhooks and APIs running 24/7 with a public URL; reliability and monthly cost dominate.

sandbox-untrusted.name: Untrusted code sandbox
sandbox-untrusted.desc: Run code you do not trust with the strongest isolation, offline by default, thrown away.

rec.strongHelp: microVM / VM / gVisor: safe for untrusted code
rec.perSecondHelp: Billed per second, deleted when the box ends
rec.forkHint: The agent will clone the box to try several paths in parallel

clone.hint: Copy-on-write copy on the same host in seconds
clone.onlyLive: Only running or sleeping boxes can be cloned
clone.title: Clone {slug}
clone.desc: A copy-on-write copy on the same host: files and installed packages are there at once, no snapshot download.

resume.title: Resume
resume.jobs: {n, plural, one {# running job} other {# running jobs}}
resume.next: Suggested next steps for the agent
resume.sleeping: The box is asleep. Loading the summary wakes it.

tierHelp.T1: Raw server/VM: boxd + Incus, billed hourly or monthly
tierHelp.T2: Sandbox API: boxd runs inside the sandbox and dials in to Core; full terminal and snapshots
tierHelp.T3: Exec-only API: a gateway shim answers for boxd; no terminal or egress rules; snapshots are tarballs kept by the gateway, preview URLs where the provider has them, otherwise a public URL via Boxaz ingress or an in-box tunnel

verHelp.live: Called the real API with a real key (read-only)
verHelp.docs: Routes and fields from the official docs/OpenAPI; not run live
verHelp.sdk: No published REST reference: read from the official SDK source

sbx.estPriceHelp: The provider does not publish per-second unit rates; Boxaz uses an estimate

cap.bootHelp: Typical time from create to running
cap.shared: Shared-kernel containers: not for untrusted code

mode.label: How boxd runs
mode.noDial: This provider cannot keep a background process, so it runs as a shim (T3) only.

modeHelp.auto: T2 when the sandbox keeps background processes and BOXAZ_PUBLIC_URL is set, else T3
modeHelp.dial: boxd runs in the sandbox and calls Core: terminal, snapshots, egress
modeHelp.shim: Core calls the exec API instead of boxd: no public URL needed, fewer features

sbx.adapterHelp: native = adapter written in Go; YAML = declarative adapter
sbx.title: Sandbox API providers
sbx.desc: Sandboxes bill per second: one sandbox per box, deleted with the box. Good for short tasks, untrusted code or fast forks. Prices and capabilities come from the adapter; the verification level says how far it has been checked.

modal.name: Modal
modal.why: SDK-only (Python/JS over Modal’s own gRPC); no public REST API for Core to call.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare Sandbox
cloudflare.why: Runs inside your own Worker (Durable Object + SDK); there is no hosted REST control plane for Core.

koyeb.name: Koyeb
koyeb.why: Sandboxes are in public preview, created via SDK/CLI with exec over a WebSocket stream; no stable REST yet.

zipbox.name: zipbox
zipbox.why: API and unit prices not verified in this release; can be added as a custom YAML adapter.

sbx.perSecondHelp: Sandboxes bill per second and are deleted when the box ends

adapter.title: Custom YAML adapter
adapter.desc: Add a new sandbox API without writing Go: declare HTTP routes, auth and JSON paths, then lint it before loading it into Core.
adapter.how1: Write the YAML from the sample (create/get/delete/exec routes, auth, capabilities, prices).
adapter.how2: Lint it here, then save the file into <mono>BOXAZ_SANDBOX_ADAPTERS_DIR</mono>.
adapter.how3: Restart Core; the new provider appears under Sandbox API, ready to connect.

ports.wakeHint: A request to the Boxaz URL wakes a sleeping box, holds the request until the app is ready, then answers it.
ports.wakeOff: Wake on request is off: requests to a sleeping box get 503
ports.title: Ports
ports.intro: Each exposed port gets a stable Boxaz URL that wakes the box on the first request and passes WebSocket/SSE through. Make it token-only to share it safely.
ports.emptyDesc: Start a server on 0.0.0.0:PORT in the box, then expose the port here.
ports.nowToken: Port {port} now needs a URL token
ports.previewCaveat: The token protects the Boxaz URL only. The provider's own preview URL for this port still answers at the provider for anyone who knows the sandbox id.

kindHint.provider-preview: The provider's own preview host (E2B, Novita, Daytona).
kindHint.ingress: Reached through Boxaz core and the in-box ingress agent.
kindHint.tunnel: An in-box Cloudflare quick tunnel (last resort).
kindHint.gateway: Only handed out through the Boxaz gateway because the port needs a token.
kindHint.none: Nothing reaches this port from the internet yet.

caps.unknown: No capability data for this provider.
caps.memory_pauseHint: Sleep keeps memory and processes; otherwise processes restart on wake.
caps.wake_on_http_nativeHint: The provider's own URL wakes a paused box.
caps.wake_via_gatewayHint: The Boxaz gateway URL wakes the box.
caps.forkHint: Native fork or clone of a live box.
caps.inbound_httpHint: The provider exposes ports to the internet itself.
caps.maxRuntimeHint: Longest continuous runtime the provider allows.

token.title: URL token for port {port}
token.desc: An expiring, revocable token for this box and port only. It never shares provider credentials.
token.once: Copy it now: the token value is shown only once.
token.label: Label
token.switchesAccess: Issuing a token switches the port to token only.
token.revokeDesc: Anyone using it loses access at once.

app.title: App
app.restartDesc: The supervisor stops the app and starts it again; gateway traffic waits until it is ready.
app.noneDesc: Declare one with box app set (CLI), the box_app_set MCP tool or PUT app in the API: Boxaz runs it, restarts it on crash and starts it again after wake, restore or clone.
app.truncatedHint: The ring buffer rotated; only recent output is kept.

ports.previewPrivate: The provider's own preview URL for this port refuses direct traffic (private sandbox): only this Boxaz URL reaches the app.
ports.name: Name
ports.nameHint: The bare name serves the primary port (demo-app.example.com); other ports get name-label (demo-app-api.example.com). Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
ports.label: Label
ports.aliasHint: The old key-port address keeps working.
ports.guessable: Name URLs are easy to guess. Turn on “Require token” for private apps.

gateway.title: Gateway domain
gateway.desc: Box URLs on your own domain with readable names (demo-app.example.com, demo-app-api.example.com), through a wildcard DNS record (e.g. a Cloudflare Tunnel, see deploy/cloudflare-tunnel).
gateway.domainHint: Bare domain, e.g. example.com. Empty = path-based URLs under BOXAZ_PUBLIC_URL.
gateway.previewHint: auto = private when the gateway is reachable from the internet. Private: new E2B / Novita sandboxes refuse direct traffic to their preview host; only the gateway (which adds the sandbox traffic token) gets in.
gateway.reserved: Reserved subdomains (never routed to a box)
gateway.guessable: Name URLs are guessable: use token mode (URL tokens) for private apps.

access.commandsDesc: Copy and run on your machine (needs the box CLI, logged in).
access.cliHint: Every command fetches its own single-use ticket (60 s) through the API; the API key never goes into a URL.
access.sshConfigDesc: Add to ~/.ssh/config to use ssh, scp, VS Code / Cursor Remote-SSH.
access.writeConfig: Or let the CLI write it
access.forwardPortsDesc: Ports box forward / ssh -L may reach. Exposed ports and the internal SSH port are always allowed.
access.forwardHint: box forward adds the port when needed (allow=true). Up to 32 extra ports per box.
access.ticketsDesc: Single-use tickets for terminal, TCP and SSH. Revoking one closes the sessions using it right away.
access.revokeAllTitle: Revoke every ticket of this box?
access.revokeAllDesc: Every terminal, forward and SSH session opened with a ticket is closed at once. Connections using an API key are not affected.
access.ticketsHint: Only a prefix and a hash are stored; the ticket value is returned once, when it is created.

linkHint.boxd: boxd in the box keeps a link to Core

sshKeys.title: SSH keys
sshKeys.desc: Public keys the SSH gateway accepts for your boxes (instead of a ticket when you ssh directly).
sshKeys.addDesc: Paste the contents of a .pub file (one line). Only the public key and fingerprint are stored.
sshKeys.name: Name
sshKeys.publicKeyHint: For example: cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub — or run box ssh-key add.
sshKeys.emptyDesc: Optional: box ssh uses a single-use ticket on its own.
sshKeys.deleteDesc: This key will no longer be able to SSH into boxes.
sshKeys.hint: Compare the host key fingerprint before trusting it the first time. CLI: box ssh-key ls | add | rm.
